messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — BigCorp asked for a routing override so some of their traffic goes to a dedicated pool for lower latency. They want this based on a customer-fingerprint header they control. Any immediate red flags?

Maria Gomez: Header-based is ok but only if it's not trivially spoofable. Prefer an HMAC-signed fingerprint header tied to a per-customer key. Example: 

```
x-redwood-org-fingerprint: org=bigcorp;v=1;sig=BASE64SIG
```

Gateway verifies sig against KMS-stored key and then checks policy DB.

TJ: Agree on sigs. Also we need to be explicit about match precedence in the routing table — header matches, path matches, method. If we don't define precedence you'll get weird tiebreakers. Also watch cache-key impact for the runtime. Quick Envoy-style example: 

```
- match:
    headers:
      - name: x-redwood-org-fingerprint
        safe_regex:
          google_re2: {}
          regex: "org=bigcorp;.*"
  route:
    cluster: bigcorp-dedicated
```

Raj Patel: Audit/telemetry note: every time an override is applied we must emit an audit span with override_id, approver, and TTL. Also tag metrics so we can compare p50/p95/99 for overridden vs normal traffic. We should also log original route decision for postmortem.

Sophia Liu: From the Console POV: we need an "Exception Request" flow — requestor gives justification, selects target pool, TTL (default 72h), and required approvers. The console should show projected perf/cost delta and give a one-click revoke. Also show who last extended the exception.

Alex Chen: Two concerns: (1) default-allow vs default-deny. I prefer default-deny — presence of header alone should not grant override unless policy DB allows that org/fingerprint. (2) Quotas — if dedicated pool runs out, we need an automatic fallback to avoid 504s. What do people think?

Maria Gomez: +1 default-deny. Implementation idea: policy table entries = {org_id, fingerprint_hash, priority, expires_at, reviewers}. Gateway flow: check policy table first -> verify signature -> route. Also add a bypass_count column for exceptional manual overrides so ops can track frequency.

TJ: For quotas and safety we should implement a phased rollout: 0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> full. Metric name: `route_override_applied{org,override_id,phase}`. Also include a simple backpressure rule: if target pool CPU > 80% or queue latency > X, automatically fall back and increment an incident counter.

Raj Patel: Security must include key rotation. Store per-customer HMAC keys in KMS, rotate quarterly. If a customer can't sign, we can fall back to verifying org JWT issued by a Redwood service account, but that should be discouraged. Also add an allowlist admin token option if enterprise wants direct admin bypasss (must be auditable).

Sophia Liu: Console details: admin list view with filters (status, expiry, org), inline telemetry link that jumps to the per-route dashboard, action buttons to extend/terminate, and an approvals history pane. UX should surface cost delta (estimated qps & token/sec) before approval.

Alex Chen: Sounds good. Next steps: prototype header verification + policy check in gateway, sketch policy DB schema + migration, and console mockups + audit schema. Who can pick which?

TJ: I'll take the gateway prototype. Will open a draft PR with an Envoy filter + unit tests by EOD Thu. I'll include feature-flag gating for canary.

Maria Gomez: I'll own the policy DB schema and migration plan. I'll post a proposed schema and example queries tomorrow.

Raj Patel: I'll draft the audit schema and telemetry labels, and a logging plan so we can trace an override end-to-end.

Sophia Liu: I'll mock the console screens and flow, wireframes in Figma, and demo to PM next week.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled for test cluster on Wed 07:00 UTC :clock7: — will require TJ's PR to be merged to the feature branch.

Alex Chen: Great. Keep updates here, and if anyone runs into policy/edge cases (e.g., cross-org proxies, CDN rewriting headers) flag them early. :thumbsup:
